scope: Read-only CPU clock boot-chain source audit and isolated read-only diagnostic module. No board/serial access or CPU PLL/PMIC writes by this agent. No production GPU build changes.

kernel.cpu_dt: boards/t736-mainline-bringup.dts:27-34 declares A55 CPUs0..5 and A76 CPUs6..7 with PSCI, but no CPU clock/OPP/cpu-supply nodes
kernel.consequence: No cpufreq governor can raise inherited CPU clocks. Current CPU MHz cannot be inferred from peripheral fixed clocks, BogoMIPS or architectural timer frequency.

boot_chain.finding: Inspected wrappers configure UART, timer, DDR/peripheral supplies and memory clocks; no explicit CPU PLL/mux initialization was found. PCLK/PERI/AHB/APB logs are not CPU frequency evidence.

Clock-related exported symbols include ccm_set_pll_ddr0_sscg, _ccm_set_pll_ddr_clk, mctl_sys_init and init_DRAM. Focused mctl_sys_init disassembly references DDR/MBUS/main-CCU addresses 0x02002588,0x02002584,0x02002c0c,0x0a020010,0x02002c00,0x02002580,0x02002020; none is CPU_PLL_CFG 0x08870000. Symbol/address search alone is not proof that every library path leaves CPU clocks unchanged.

Native PSCI is selected, SCPI/ARISC and regulator setup disabled; platform sunxi_pmic_setup returns0. No CPU PLL frequency configuration found in applicable platform/common path. AHB200MHz writes in common setup are gated to A64, not A733/T736. CPU interconnect reset/gate writes do not program CPU frequency.

TARGET_T736_BRINGUP=y; ARCH_CPU_INIT=n (69), ARCH_SUNXI=n (122), CLOCKS=n (409), CPU=n (790). board/t736/bringup/board.c board_init:53 returns0; enable_caches:64 enables I/D cache. The generic sunxi SPL clock setup is not selected by this custom chain.

diagnostic.behavior: Init-only ioremap/readl snapshot of 20 documented CPU clock CTRL/PAT/LFM/MUX/CTRL_STAT/SLOW registers; no MMIO writes, clock registration, clock enable, reset, regulator operation or vendor CCF callback. Raw values only because manual and vendor formula discrepancies require explicit interpretation. Rmmod has no hardware operation.
diagnostic.offset_peer_review: event_review confirmed all20 offsets documented, aligned and within0x4000; PAT1 SDM_BUSY is read-only, CTRL26 R/WAC triggers only on write; no read-clear semantics.

interpretation: A55_CLK/A76_CLK[26:24] 0,1,2 select CPU_SLOW;3 selects associated CPU PLL with external divider;4 selects PERI0PLL_DIV2;5 selects CPU_BACK. CPU_SLOW_CLK[1:0]0=DCXO,1=32K,2=16M_RC. DSU mux4/5 and CTRL_STAT N formula conflict across sources: preserve raw values and do not assert an actual frequency without resolving selection/factors.
status: Strong source-level reason to investigate inherited CPU rate; no runtime CPU rate was measured in this audit and no claim that low CPU frequency caused all desktop flicker.
next_step: Root owns hardware: sample runtime mux/PLL registers using the isolated module; inspect thermal/regulator/voltage constraints before proposing CPU clock writes. Do not use a fixed software clock node to claim a hardware rate.
